chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One who guarantees four [things] with four [verses/concepts] will be in Paradise: Spend and do not fear poverty, and be just to people regarding yourself, and spread peace throughout the world, and avoid argument even if you are right.

key_terms.أَبْيَاتٍ: verses or stanzas (metaphorically referring to distinct points or verses)

ai.seo_question: What are the four guaranteed actions for entering Paradise according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links spiritual security to four practical virtues: spending without fear of poverty, self-restraint in judgment, spreading peace, and avoiding argumentation even when right. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and *hilm* (forbearance) as essential components of faith, ensuring that one's correctness does not lead to social discord. The guarantee of Paradise serves as a powerful motivator for integrating these ethical behaviors into daily communal life.

en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that one who is ready to guarantee to do four things will get four guaranteed homes in Paradise. They are: spending (for deserving causes) without fear from poverty, yielding to justice for people even against one’s own-self, offering greetings of peace loud and clearly in the world, and avoiding unneeded arguments, even if one is on the right side.”
